answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A knoll of fresh accounts then demands fresh capital for every account; splitting one stake across identities does not multiply voting weight or payouts. If an account is caught double-spending or colluding, its stake is slashed, while honest agents recover theirs after a delay. The orchard of identities is therefore costly to plant and easy to prune, and a pearl-sized stake cannot buy a crowd.
